purpose: Base capability measurement at Qwen3-Next-80B-A3B-Instruct for slm-learning ladder extension. Per slm-learning-210 + teacher_species_policy.md, this is the strongest open-weight rung we plan to evaluate as a backbone candidate — 80B total / 3.9B active per token (MoE, hybrid Transformer-Mamba) gives ~7B-equivalent inference latency at H100-class memory. Owned-domain delta vs 7B Stein canonical is the key signal.
fire_command_template: MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1 PYTHONIOENCODING=utf-8 modal run modal_app/eval_adapter.py::main --adapter-id BASE --base-model Qwen/Qwen3-Next-80B-A3B-Instruct --benchmark {benchmark} --limit 164 --gpu H100 --persist-run-id eval-base-qwen3-next-80b-a3b-2026-05-09
fallback_quant: FP8 if H100 capacity-constrained on Modal; INT4 introduces quality skew that breaks the comparison and is REJECTED. If neither H100 nor FP8 path is available, defer this rung.

pass_criteria.knee_candidate: HE >= 0.910 AND MBPP >= 0.880 AND gad_tools delta vs 7B Stein > +5pp
pass_criteria.promote_to_training_target: knee_candidate AND active-param latency demonstrably < 1.5x 7B-dense at chat-mode N=164
pass_criteria.reject_rung: HE delta vs 32B base < +2pp OR gad_tools regression vs 7B Stein

preflight_notes: DO NOT FIRE without Dr. Stein authorization. H100 availability on Modal must be verified live (capacity is bursty). 80B-A3B BF16 weights are ~160GB on disk; slm-models volume MUST be checked first or the download alone will burn budget. Hybrid Transformer-Mamba MoE may need a recent vLLM/transformers pin — verify modal_app eval image transformers>=4.50 actually supports the architecture before firing.
